note: The end-to-end product path, and the measurement everything else has been extrapolated from: real portal capture of a live window (a GeForce Now stream), the display on, shared memory, pixels saved. Every number on record used --source synthetic, so the input leg has never been measured in this pipeline; the portal leg alone reads ~19 ms stocked and up to 159 ms dribbling, which is over the entire 16.7 ms budget before the worker starts. Run it with /opt/neuralscreen/run_manually.sh from a terminal in the graphical session and click the portal dialog. Read, in order: the capture split (wait vs read), the client stage means, and the steady median. If the capture split shows read ~19 ms, the product frame time is worker 22 + client 4 + capture 19 - no amount of worker work reaches 60 fps and the input path becomes the programme.
